restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r6-prefix-v1 only (six partial rounds plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction uses the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

Success probability 1 means: one deterministic procedure (centres c_i = i tried in the order i = 1, 2, 3, ... until the first collision) was executed once from the start on the fixed target and stopped with a collision after 3 trials; the time is the executed operation count of that run with every trial charged, failed ones included, and the memory its static image plus the stack bounds. It is not a probability over centres; no start was selected beforehand.

The operation count is the work summed over the 20 threads of the run (the cost model charges total work, not latency); the thread count changes only the declared thread charges (proof.md section 4.5).

heuristics.statement: The counts of proof.md sections 6 and 7 describe the executed program of proof.md section 9 under the stated rules: 1 per field operation (a Montgomery conversion is one multiplication; inversion and exponentiation expanded), 1 per element load or store plus 1 address operation, 3 per loop iteration plus 2 per loop exit (the loops written with the macro FOR8 are unrolled eight times in the source and charged 3 per pass of eight; the transform kernels are generated straight-line code), 1 per other executed index or control operation, 342 per line evaluation or reference hash, 200 per active thread and 10 per chunk of every parallel region as the declared cost of thread control, fixed bounds for the progress lines, the report formatting, the system calls and the stage bookkeeping, and a register file of 18 words of 256 bits per transform block (16 data words, the twiddle operand and one temporary) as the only register assumption.
heuristics.scope: All stages of the executed run of proof.md section 4 at the target dimensions (m = 122,070,312; transforms of length L = 2^27; 2^28 line evaluations per trial; 20 threads).
heuristics.extrapolation: None. The time is the executed total of one run of the shipped source, with every trial charged and the allocator, the progress lines, the report formatting, the write calls and the exit charged; the only bounds in it are the stated per-byte, per-stage, per-thread and system-call constants of proof.md section 4.2, each charged in full.
heuristics.limitations: The counts are produced by the instrumentation written into the source; the source is part of the proof text and was not run by the organizer. The declared thread charges stand in for the pthread wake and join machinery and the one-time creation of the worker threads; word-level costs outside the stated rules (cache, bandwidth, the kernel scheduling of sleeping workers) are not part of the model.
